# `io` standard library

The `io` module provides high-performance, buffered input and formatted output
for file descriptors, standard streams, and sockets.

```dva
#use io
```

## Standard descriptors and output

| Descriptor | Value | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `io::STDIN` | `0` | Standard input |
| `io::STDOUT` | `1` | Standard output |
| `io::STDERR` | `2` | Standard error |

### Standard status and error constants

| Constant | Value | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `io::EOF` | `0` | Stream end-of-file |
| `io::EINTR` | `4` | Interrupted system call (retried automatically by `io` operations) |
| `io::EBADF` | `9` | Bad file descriptor |
| `io::EAGAIN` | `11` | Resource temporarily unavailable / would block |
| `io::EWOULDBLOCK` | `11` | Alias for `io::EAGAIN` |

### Output functions

| Function | Signature | Description | Example |
|---|---|---|---|
| `io::out(x)` | `#! T: Type, T => ()` | Prints value or space-separated record + newline to `STDOUT` | `io::out(("Result:", 42))` |
| `io::err(x)` | `#! T: Type, T => ()` | Prints value or space-separated record + newline to `STDERR` | `io::err(("Error:", code))` |
| `io::outf(val, fmt)` | `#! T: Type, T, String => ()` | Formatted output to `STDOUT` replacing `{}` placeholders with value | `io::outf((10, <+>), "Val: {}, Flag: {}")` |
| `io::errf(val, fmt)` | `#! T: Type, T, String => ()` | Formatted output to `STDERR` replacing `{}` placeholders with value | `io::errf(line, "Failed at line {}")` |
| `io::write(fd, s)` | `Int, String => Int` | Raw length-aware write of String `s` to descriptor `fd`, returns bytes written | `io::write(io::STDOUT, "raw\n")` |

```dva
#use io

// Multi-argument printing (records print space-separated):
io::out(("Server starting on port", 8080))

// Placeholder formatting:
io::outf(("127.0.0.1", 9000), "Client connected from {}:{}")
```

## Buffered `Reader` API

`io::reader(fd)` wraps a file descriptor in a buffered reader (default buffer 4096 bytes).
All read methods return the optional ramification `< String | >` or `< Int | >`,
where the positive branch carries available data and the absent branch `<-->`
indicates that no data is currently available (due to EOF, nonblocking would-block, or error):

| Function | Signature | Return Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `io::reader(fd)` | `Int => Reader` | `Reader` | Creates Reader with default 4 KB buffer |
| `io::reader_with_cap(fd, cap)` | `Int, Int => Reader` | `Reader` | Creates Reader with custom buffer size |
| `io::read(r, max)` | `Reader, Int => < String | >` | `< String | >` | Reads available buffer chunk up to `max` bytes |
| `io::read_all(r, max)` | `Reader, Int => < String | >` | `< String | >` | Drains stream completely up to `max` bytes |
| `io::read_byte(r)` | `Reader => < Int | >` | `< Int | >` | Reads next byte code (`0..255`) or `<-->` |
| `io::read_until(r, delim, max)`| `Reader, Int, Int => < String | >`| `< String | >` | Reads until delimiter byte is encountered |
| `io::read_line(r, max)` | `Reader, Int => < String | >` | `< String | >` | Reads until newline (`\n` or `\r\n`) |

### Reader state inspection

When a read operation returns `<-->`, inspect the reader's state to distinguish between EOF,
would-block on nonblocking descriptors, and unhandled read errors:

| Function | Signature | Return Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `io::reader_eof(r)` | `Reader => <>` | `<>` | True (`<+>`) if clean EOF has been reached |
| `io::reader_err(r)` | `Reader => Int` | `Int` | Returns errno of the last I/O failure (0 if none) |
| `io::reader_would_block(r)` | `Reader => <>` | `<>` | True (`<+>`) if the last read on a nonblocking fd would block (`EAGAIN`/`EWOULDBLOCK`) |
| `io::reader_has_err(r)` | `Reader => <>` | `<>` | True (`<+>`) if an unhandled read error occurred (`err != 0`) |
| `io::reader_clear(r)` | `Reader => ()` | `()` | Resets error and EOF state flags on reader |

### Nonblocking contract

On nonblocking file descriptors (`O_NONBLOCK`), when no data is ready:
- Read methods return the absent branch `<-->`.
- `io::reader_would_block(r)` evaluates to `<+>`.
- `io::reader_err(r)` is set to `io::EAGAIN` (`11`).
- `io::reader_eof(r)` evaluates to `<->`.

Callers can check `io::reader_would_block(r)` to yield or wait on readiness notifications (such as `epoll` or `poll`),
resuming read operations once data arrives. Interrupted calls (`EINTR`) are automatically retried internally.

## Buffered input examples

### Reading line by line

```dva
#use io

r = io::reader(io::STDIN)

0.. @
   line_res = io::read_line(r, 1024)
   line_res
      | line => io::outf(line, "Echo: {}")
      | --> // Break on EOF or error
```

### Distinguishing EOF, Would-Block, and Errors

```dva
#use io

r = io::reader(fd)

0.. @
   chunk = io::read(r, 4096)
   chunk
      | data =>
         io::outf(?data, "Received {} bytes")
      |
         io::reader_would_block(r)
            | --> // Descriptor would block; wait for poll/epoll readiness
         io::reader_eof(r)
            |
               io::out("Clean EOF reached")
               -->
         // Unhandled error (e.g. EBADF, EIO)
         io::errf(io::reader_err(r), "Read failed with errno: {}")
         -->
```

### Reading with unwrap-or-abort (`!!`)

When expecting a mandatory header or fixed payload where absence represents an unrecoverable failure:

```dva
#use io

r = io::reader(fd)
header = io::read_line(r, 256)!! // Aborts with stack trace if EOF or error reached
io::out("Received header: " + header)
```
